rules.problem: Structure (any of rest pain / ulcer / gangrene) is the natural reading of the comma list. One gap to confirm at runtime: a patient recorded only with the three-qualifier finding from the first bullet (sudden, severe, at rest) and none of numbness/weakness/pallor/no pulse will not match the acute rule, and will match this rule only if the engine treats the more-qualified 'Pain in lower limb' as satisfying the 'At rest'-only form. If qualifier matching is exact, that patient gets no diagnosis at all although the page says leg pain at rest alone makes critical limb ischaemia likely.

summary: All 38 claims are faithful to the page: every red-box criterion, the three 'likely' diagnoses and the one 'possible' diagnosis (AAA from a pulsatile mass) are encoded with the right structure, trigger and priority level, and every SNOMED concept exists. The only point worth confirming is whether a leg-pain finding recorded with sudden+severe+at-rest qualifiers also satisfies the at-rest-only condition in the critical limb ischaemia rule; if qualifier matching is exact, a patient with sudden severe rest pain but none of numbness/weakness/pallor/no pulse would get no diagnosis. Two concepts are best-available approximations rather than exact matches ('White discoloration of skin' for pallor, 'Weakness of muscle of lower limb' for weakness); no closer concept exists in this release.
